- Priya (Acme) — late afternoons CEST (15:00–18:00 CEST)

Evan — thanks for the MAP and context. Quick summary and concrete options below. Note: US/CEST/AEST transitions are different — to avoid confusion I converted everything to UTC and then to each local zone.

High-level constraints from our execs:
- US (Mark, SVP Product): prefers 10:00–12:00 PT (UTC-7 during our current DST)
- EU (Sofia, Head of Sales EMEA): available 15:00–17:00 CEST (UTC+2)
- APAC (Ken, Head of Engineering APAC): can do mornings Sydney time (09:00–11:00 AEST, UTC+10) but not late evenings local

Option A (single live window — best for execs overlap):
- UTC 15:00 — corresponds to 08:00 PT / 17:00 CEST / 01:00 AEST (next day) — BAD for APAC (overnight)

Option B (single live with two execs + recorded bridge — recommended):
- Live: UTC 16:00 — 09:00 PT (US), 18:00 CEST (EU), 02:00 AEST (APAC) — still late for APAC
- Proposal: live session focused on US+EU execs (45 min), record first 20 minutes (intro + demo), schedule a 30-min APAC-only live Q&A the next morning in APAC local time.

Option C (split-session approach — balanced):
- Session 1 (US/EU focused): UTC 15:30 — 08:30 PT / 17:30 CEST (45 min, exec intro + product deep-dive)
- Session 2 (APAC friendly): next day UTC 00:30 — 17:30 PT / 02:30 CEST / 10:30 AEST (30 min live Q&A and tailored content for APAC execs).

DST note: US transitions earlier in the fall/spring than EU; when we send calendar invites, include an explicit line like “Meeting times shown in UTC for clarity: 2029-10-27T15:30Z” to avoid auto-conversion errors. For now our dates are in May (both sides on DST) but it's caused issues historically when follow-ups are scheduled into October/November.

Next actions:
- Evan/Priya: pick Option B (single live with recorded intro + APAC Q&A) or Option C (split sessions), or suggest a firm UTC slot.
- We will prepare the recorded intro (20m) and a separate APAC Q&A deck if needed.
- I attached calendar .ics placeholders for the two proposals (Proposed-Exec-Slots.ics).

If you confirm, I can send formal calendar invites with explicit UTC times and clear locale conversions.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick suggestion from Solutions EMEA/APAC perspective (Soojin):

If Acme wants full exec representation without anyone staying awake past midnight, we usually run a hybrid pattern:
1) 45 min US+EU live (exec intros + strategic demo). Record first 20–25 minutes verbatim.
2) Provide recording and a 2-page exec summary to all.
3) Schedule a 30–45 minute APAC-friendly session the next local morning with the same demo owner and one APAC lead from Acme — make that session explicitly "Q&A + infra deep dive."

Concrete times (proposed for week of Jun 17 — all shown in UTC / US PT / CEST / AEST):
- US/EU live (recommended): UTC 15:30 — 08:30 PT / 17:30 CEST / 01:30 AEST (next day) — record first 25m.
- APAC Q&A: UTC 23:30 next day — 16:30 PT / 01:30 CEST / 10:30 AEST (good APAC morning).

I know the 01:30 AEST for the US/EU combo is awkward for APAC; that’s why we record and do the APAC live Q&A morning the next day. This pattern has worked for two large customers without exec fatigue.

I'll prep the two invites with explicit UTC times and include a line in the invite description: "All times shown in UTC to avoid DST auto-conversion issues: please cross-check local time before accepting."

Soojin Lee
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
